hooks._note: Above gates.TEST_TIMEOUT (240s). If the two matched, this hook could be killed before the script returned its timeout denial — and a gate that dies lets the commit through.

Holds /forge:start back when the plugin is stale, and hands over the exact command. start.md already said to check, and rule R13 is what it is — an instruction the model can skip is advice. Starting on an old build writes a notes layout and a question sequence shaped by the wrong version. Says nothing for every other prompt, and 'anyway' gets past it.

The installed copy lagged the repository for four sessions running, and every one of them began by debugging the wrong build. Checks once a day, caches the answer outside the plugin so a reinstall does not reset it, and says nothing on any failure. FORGE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 turns it off.

Brings ponytail in with Forge rather than leaving it in a routing table nothing is obliged to read (decision 059). One line when it is installed, the install command once per project when it is not, silence on every error and outside a Forge project. FORGE_NO_COMPANION=1 turns it off.

The governor gates writes, which are a file path a hook can see. This gates speech. Rules R10 and R12 lived only in the prompts until a run put a decision on screen as three unframed paragraphs and nothing could tell. Fails open on everything: a blocked write costs a turn, a wedged Stop hook costs the session.
